Sue Couter (Immediate Media - Senior Strategy Food Partnerships I Food judge I MIX 92.6 food correspondent)
This week, after more than 13 incredible years, the time has come to say farewell to Tesco. It’s been one heck of a ride and I’m super proud of my contributions to the food, health and social impact space. 

When I started back in Tesco’s Media Publishing Centre in 2013, my teens were toddlers, and now we are knee-deep in exams. I loved those early years in Mount Farm’s creative studio, working with so many talented writers, designers and photographers. 

Over the years, I moved into the food education space, a dream role following my professional cookery training. The long-running Eat Happy programme connected millions of primary school children with stores, farms and factories to help young people understand the origins of food, building positive associations through direct + sensory experiences. The Online Field Trips were pioneering for their time (years before Covid), connecting classrooms with growers, farmers and suppliers for interactive educational sessions. 

It’s also been a real privilege to work closely with the UK’s leading health charities to help raise awareness and vital funding, and support prevention for some of the nation’s most prevalent health conditions, including type 2 diabetes, heart diseases and cancers. Together, we also held some of the biggest fundraisers and colleague engagement events, including 4,500 keen walkers going from Land’s End to John O’Groats – and we even broke the Guiness World Record for 30 hours of consecutive dance at Wembley Stadium! It’s no overstatement to say that Tesco folks have great moves. 💃 🕺

Supporting food allergy awareness has been important and emotional work. I have the utmost respect for Tanya and Nadim, campaigning relentlessly to change the allergy landscape. 

My role campaigning for healthy and sustainable diets has been a natural extension of my upbringing and training. It can be tricky to reconcile my influences from the Med, the US and the UK, but ultimately, it all goes back to the joys of seasonal everyday whole foods as the foundation. If you follow me here, you’ll know that I share a fair bit (maybe too much 😉) about good food, food culture and food experiences, and you can also find me doing that on Insta. A friend recently described me as a ‘food enthusiast’, which I’ll happily take. 

To the amazing colleagues across Tesco – you’ve made me laugh, cry and everything in between. Thank you for your great energy and spirit. 

To the many wonderful external partners I’ve worked closely with over the years – thank you for sharing your expertise and friendship: British Heart Foundation Cancer Research UK (CRUK) Diabetes UK British Nutrition Foundation The Natasha Allergy Research Foundation British Red Cross The Jamie Oliver Group Bite Back Future Food Movement The Food Foundation Veg Power CIC

So while it’s the end of an amazing era, it’s also the start of many wonderful new chapters. Take good care of yourselves and have a fabulous summer. Now back to my rosé…🥂💚
